docs.title: AlphaFloor EFB User Guide
docs.text:
Welcome to the AlphaFloor EFB user guide. AlphaFloor EFB is a modern Universal Electronic Flight Bag designed for X-Plane 12. It provides comprehensive operational flight planning, performance calculations, aircraft weight and balance management, charts, checklists, documents, weather radar, and ground servicing tools.

AlphaFloor EFB can be operated directly inside a 3D cockpit tablet, in a native 2D floating popup window, or streamed over your local network to any tablet, iPad, phone, or secondary computer.

docs.title: Supported Aircraft
docs.text: AlphaFloor EFB works across all X-Plane 12 aircraft via its modular Aircraft Adaptation Layer, native 2D floating popup window, and remote Wi-Fi tablet streaming. In addition, dedicated airframe profiles, custom 3D cockpit integrations, and tailored operational checklists are provided for:

docs.title: Commercial Airliners
docs.text:
• ToLiss A319
  • ToLiss A320 & A320neo
  • ToLiss A321, A321neo, A321LR & A321XLR
  • ToLiss A330-900
  • ToLiss A340-600
  • Laminar Research Airbus A330-300 (featuring native 3D tablet injection via the X-Plane Avionics API)

docs.title: General Aviation
docs.text:
• Aerobask Diamond DA42 NG (native 3D tablet cockpit integration, tailored ground handling, and operational checklists)
  • Airfoillabs Cessna 172 Digital & Laminar Research Cessna 172 (tailored GA ground operations, tie-downs, engine covers, and full checklists)

docs.title: Universal Fleet
docs.text: • All other X-Plane 12 Aircraft: Operates with universal weight and fuel loading, ground operations, SimBrief OFP dispatch, Navigraph charts, live weather and radar, checklists, documents, and web browser.

docs.title: Operating Modes
docs.text:
1. 3D Virtual Cockpit Tablet: Renders directly onto compatible 3D cockpit tablets (config.json or AviTab.json) with native 3D mouse capture. On aircraft lacking an existing 3D tablet mesh, AlphaFloor EFB can inject a standalone 3D tablet model directly into the cockpit via the Avionics API.
  2. 2D Floating Popup Window: Open a resizable 2D floating EFB window in any aircraft via Plugins > AlphaFloor EFB > Show EFB Window or the AlphaFloorEFB/toggle_window keybind command.
  3. External Device (Wi-Fi LAN Streaming): Connect your iPad, Android tablet, phone, or secondary computer to the same local network as your simulation PC. Open the network address displayed in the EFB Settings to control the EFB with responsive touch controls.

docs.title: Quick Navigation
docs.text:
• Installation Guide: How to install and verify the plugin.
  • Licensing & Free Trial: Starting your 7-day free trial, purchasing a lifetime license, and multi-device activation.
  • Interface & Controls: Cockpit interaction, window controls, and remote web access.
  • Applications Guide: Step-by-step instructions for each built-in EFB application.
  • Troubleshooting: Solutions for common setup and network issues.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
This guide walks you through installing AlphaFloor EFB into X-Plane 12, verifying the setup, and configuring external tablet connections over your local network.

The AviTab plugin should be disabled when using AlphaFloor EFB to avoid any unexpected interactions.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
• Flight Simulator: X-Plane 12 (version 12.00 or later).
  • Operating System:
  • Windows: Windows 10 or Windows 11 (64-bit).
  • macOS: macOS Monterey (12.0) or newer (Universal binary natively supporting Apple Silicon and Intel).
  • Linux: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Debian 12, Fedora 38 or equivalent 64-bit distribution with standard glibc.
  • Supported Aircraft: Any X-Plane 12 aircraft. Dedicated airframe profiles, custom 3D integrations, and tailored operational checklists are provided for:
  • Commercial Airliners: ToLiss A319, A320 & A320neo, A321, A321neo, A321LR & A321XLR, A330-900, A340-600, and Laminar Research Airbus A330-300.
  • General Aviation: Aerobask Diamond DA42 NG, Airfoillabs Cessna 172 Digital, and Laminar Research Cessna 172.
  • Universal Fleet: All other X-Plane 12 aircraft via the 2D floating popup window, AviTab 3D mesh integration, and external Wi-Fi tablet streaming.

docs.title: 1. Download the Release Archive
docs.text: Download the latest release archive (AlphaFloorEFB-vX.Y.Z.zip) from the CyberPatate Website.

docs.title: 2. Extract and Move to the Plugins Folder
docs.text:
Extract the downloaded .zip file. You will see a folder named AlphaFloorEFB.

Move the entire AlphaFloorEFB folder into your X-Plane 12 plugins directory:

X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins/AlphaFloorEFB/

Or use plugin management tools such as XLauncher.

docs.title: 3. Verify Folder Structure
docs.text:
Confirm that the folder hierarchy looks as follows:

X-Plane 12/
\-- Resources/
    \-- plugins/
        \-- AlphaFloorEFB/
            |-- mac_x64/
            |   \-- AlphaFloorEFB.xpl
            |-- win_x64/
            |   \-- AlphaFloorEFB.xpl
            |-- lin_x64/
            |   \-- AlphaFloorEFB.xpl
            |-- config.json
            |-- user_checklists.json.example
            |-- skunkcrafts_updater.cfg
            \-- user-guide.pdf

Important: Do not rename the AlphaFloorEFB folder. Keep all files in their respective subdirectories.

docs.title: First Launch & Verification
docs.text:
1. Launch X-Plane 12.
  2. From the flight setup menu, load any aircraft in X-Plane 12.
  3. Once the cockpit finishes loading, view the 3D cockpit tablet (on aircraft with 3D tablet integration) or open the 2D floating window from Plugins > AlphaFloor EFB > Show EFB Window.
  4. The tablet screen will power on and display the AlphaFloor EFB home screen.
  5. Click anywhere on the screen with your mouse to interact with the applications.

docs.title: Connecting External Devices (iPad, Android, Laptops)
docs.text:
You can use any external tablet, iPad, smartphone, or laptop as a standalone touch EFB while flying.

  1. Connect your external device to the same local Wi-Fi network as your flight simulator PC.
  2. In the 3D cockpit EFB, tap the Settings icon on the bottom navigation bar.
  3. Locate the Remote Tablet Access section. You will see an address such as: 
    http://192.168.1.42:40899
  4. Open your preferred web browser (e.g., Safari on iPad or Chrome on Android/PC) and enter that URL.
  5. The EFB interface will load with full touch functionality. Any action performed on the external device is instantly synchronized with the aircraft and the cockpit screen.

Tip for iPad users: In Safari, tap the Share button and select Add to Home Screen. This launches the EFB in full-screen mode without browser address bars.

docs.title: Updating AlphaFloor EFB
docs.text:
• Via SkunkCrafts Updater: AlphaFloor EFB includes full SkunkCrafts Updater integration. When an update is published, open your SkunkCrafts Updater client to download and apply the update. Your license file and custom checklists are automatically preserved.
  • Manual Update: Download the new .zip package from the website and overwrite the contents of X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins/AlphaFloorEFB/. Your license file (AlphaFloorEFB.lic or license.json) will remain intact.

docs.title: Screen Layout
docs.text: The tablet display is divided into three functional areas:

docs.title: 1. Top Status Bar
docs.text:
• Clock Display: Displays current simulation time.
  • Aircraft Type: Shows active aircraft variant (e.g., A319, A320neo, A321LR, A330-900, A340-600, DA42, C172).
  • Power & Indicators: Visual indicators for battery charge level and network status.
  • Minimize Button: Minimizes the 3D cockpit overlay on dual-mode tablet displays.

docs.title: 2. Main Content Area
docs.text: This central viewport displays whichever application is currently open (e.g., Performance Calculator, SimBrief OFP, Charts, or Checklists).

docs.title: 3. Bottom Navigation Bar
docs.text:
• Home Button (Left): Instantly returns to the application launcher grid from any screen.
  • Quick Access Icons (Middle): Allows switching between the main applications without returning to the home screen.
  • Settings Button (Right): Opens the system configuration panel.

docs.title: Responsive Layout & Small Tablet Adaptation
docs.text: AlphaFloor EFB automatically adapts its interface layout for different screen dimensions: * Standard Tablets & Desktop Monitors: Full multi-column view optimized for standard tablet aspect ratios and floating desktop windows. * Compact / Small Displays: Tailored compact layouts for smaller cockpit tablet mounts, smartphones, or constrained windows, maintaining high legibility and touch target accessibility.

docs.title: In-Cockpit 3D Interaction
docs.text:
• Left Click: Tap any button, tab, input field, or checklist item.
  • Double Left Click: Quick zoom in/zoom out on documents and charts.
  • Mouse Drag: Hold the left mouse button and drag to scroll through documents, charts and list items.
  • Text Input: Click inside an input field (such as an airport ICAO code or gross weight) and type directly on your physical keyboard or use the virtual keyboard.
  • 2D Floating Popup Window: Open or close the standalone 2D floating EFB window at any time from Plugins > AlphaFloor EFB > Show EFB Window or by binding a key/button to AlphaFloorEFB/toggle_window.
  • Minimizing the 3D EFB Overlay: On aircraft with a dual-mode 3D cockpit tablet, click the Minimize icon in the top status bar to temporarily hide the AlphaFloor EFB 3D overlay and access the underlying cockpit screen. To restore AlphaFloor EFB, tap the AviTab tab on the cockpit tablet screen, execute the AlphaFloorEFB/toggle_overlay command, or toggle Enable EFB Overlay in the Plugins menu.

docs.title: External Tablet & Mobile Interaction
docs.text:
When viewing the EFB on an iPad, Android tablet, phone, or laptop:

  • Tap: Equivalent to a mouse click.
  • Touch Drag: Smooth inertial scrolling through checklists, flight logs, and weather reports.
  • Pinch to Zoom: Zoom in and out of georeferenced airport diagrams and enroute charts.
  • Orientation Support: The interface automatically reorganizes its layout when switching between landscape and portrait orientations.
  • Full-Screen / Standalone Mode:
    • iPad / iOS: In Safari, tap the Share button and select Add to Home Screen. Launching AlphaFloor from the home screen icon runs it in standalone mode without Safari's address bar or navigation buttons.
    • Android / Desktop: Tap the Maximize / Fullscreen button in the top status bar (beside the battery indicator) or select Add to Home screen in your browser menu.

docs.title: Licensing & Free Trial
docs.text: AlphaFloor EFB offers a transparent, pilot-friendly licensing model. You can test every feature without restriction for seven days before deciding to purchase.

docs.title: 7-Day Free Trial
docs.text:
Every pilot is entitled to a 7-day free trial with full access to all applications and calculations.

  1. Launch X-Plane 12 with any supported Airbus aircraft.
  2. If this is your first time loading the plugin, the license prompt appears on the tablet.
  3. Click Start 7-Day Free Trial.
  4. Your trial period begins immediately. An indicator at the top of the Settings screen displays your remaining trial days.
  5. You do not need to provide a credit card, email address, or account registration to use the trial.

docs.title: Purchasing a License
docs.text:
When you are ready to purchase a permanent license:

  • Price: 11.99 € (single one-time payment, lifetime license).
  • In-app Purchase: Purchase the license directly from the EFB tablet within X-Plane 12.
  • Payment Processing: Processed securely through Stripe.
  • Updates Included: All minor and feature updates throughout the 1.x release cycle are included free of charge.

docs.title: Activating Your License
docs.text: After completing your purchase on the website, you will be redirected to an order confirmation screen. Your license is automatically validated in the EFB. You also have two alternative activation methods:

docs.title: Method 1: In-App License Key Entry
docs.text:
1. Copy the license key displayed on your confirmation screen (e.g., AFEFB-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX).
  2. In X-Plane 12, open the EFB tablet and tap the Settings icon.
  3. Select the License section.
  4. Paste or enter your key into the License Key field and click Activate.
  5. The status indicator will turn green and display Licensed (Full Version).

docs.title: Method 2: Standalone License File (AlphaFloorEFB.lic)
docs.text:
1. On your order confirmation screen, click the Download AlphaFloorEFB.lic button.
  2. Save the file directly into your plugin directory: 
    X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins/AlphaFloorEFB/AlphaFloorEFB.lic
  3. When you load the aircraft, AlphaFloor EFB automatically detects the file and activates your license without requiring manual key entry.

docs.title: Multi-Device Policy
docs.text:
• Up to 3 Personal Computers: Your purchase allows concurrent activation on up to three (3) personal computers (e.g., main flight sim desktop, laptop, secondary simulator rig) owned and operated by the same pilot.
  • External Tablets Do Not Consume Activations: iPads, Android tablets, phones, and laptops connected via local Wi-Fi to display the web interface are clients of your main simulator and do not count toward machine activations.

docs.title: Offline License Verification
docs.text: Once your license is verified, AlphaFloor EFB operates completely offline on your local computer.

docs.title: Refund Policy
docs.text: If you encounter technical defects or hardware incompatibilities that cannot be resolved within 14 calendar days of your purchase, contact support at contact@cyberpatate.fr for a prompt, full refund.

docs.title: Troubleshooting & FAQ
docs.text:
This section provides solutions for common setup questions, network connectivity, and troubleshooting tips.

The AviTab plugin should be disabled when using AlphaFloor EFB to avoid any unexpected interactions.

docs.title: My iPad or tablet cannot open the EFB web page
docs.text:
• Same Wi-Fi Network: Ensure your mobile device and simulation computer are connected to the exact same Wi-Fi router or subnet. If your phone or tablet is connected to cellular 4G/5G or a guest Wi-Fi network with client isolation enabled, it cannot reach the PC.
  • Verify IP Address: Simulation PCs can change IP addresses if your router reboots. Check the Settings screen on the cockpit tablet to confirm the current IP address.
  • Firewall Rules: Ensure your operating system firewall allows incoming TCP connections on the configured EFB port (default 40899).

docs.title: My SimBrief flight plan does not load
docs.text:
• Confirm that your SimBrief Username or Pilot ID is entered correctly in the EFB Settings without extra spaces.
  • Ensure you have actively generated an Operational Flight Plan (OFP) on SimBrief.com before clicking Fetch.
  • Verify that your simulation computer has an active internet connection.

docs.title: Navigraph charts do not display
docs.text:
• Verify that your Navigraph account has an active Charts subscription.
  • Go to Settings -> Navigraph, tap Sign Out, and complete the authentication process again using the QR code or device code.

docs.title: Profile view shows "Weather data temporarily unavailable"
docs.text:
• The profile view queries the Open-Meteo weather API to generate atmospheric soundings along your route.
  • Open-Meteo enforces request rate limits. If these limits are reached or the service is temporarily unreachable, this overlay is displayed until the limit resets. Weather data is automatically cached per flight once retrieved to avoid unnecessary requests.

docs.title: My license key shows "Invalid Key"
docs.text:
• Ensure there are no accidental spaces before or after the key when copy-pasting.
  • License keys follow the format: key/XXXX.
  • If you purchased recently, ensure your payment was completed successfully on Stripe.

docs.title: Standalone file AlphaFloorEFB.lic is not detected
docs.text:
• Verify that the file is placed directly in the main plugin folder: 
    X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins/AlphaFloorEFB/AlphaFloorEFB.lic
  • Make sure your operating system has not appended an extra extension (such as AlphaFloorEFB.lic.txt).

docs.title: Contact Support
docs.text:
If you encounter an issue not covered in this guide, our support team is available to assist:

  • Support Email: contact@cyberpatate.fr
  • Website: https://cyberpatate.fr/alphafloorefb/

docs.title: Ground Services
docs.text: The Ground Services application allows pilots to manage aircraft doors, ground servicing equipment, and external electrical power directly from the cockpit tablet. The interface dynamically adapts its schematic, door controls, and available equipment to the loaded aircraft.

docs.title: Dynamic Overhead Aircraft Schematic
docs.text: The application presents an interactive overhead schematic matching the geometry of the active aircraft:

docs.title: Passenger & Service Doors
docs.text:
• Door 1L: Main passenger boarding door (connected to jetway or boarding stairs).
  • Door 1R: Forward galley and catering service door.
  • Door 2L / 2R & 3L / 3R: Overwing emergency exits and mid-cabin doors (on extended airframes).
  • Door 4L / 4R: Aft passenger and service doors.

docs.title: Cargo Compartments
docs.text:
• Forward Cargo Door: Opens the forward lower hold for luggage containers and pallets.
  • Aft Cargo Door: Opens the aft lower hold.
  • Bulk Cargo Door: Opens the rear bulk compartment.

docs.title: Quick Actions & Automated Sequencing
docs.text:
• All Doors Open: Opens all passenger and cargo doors simultaneously for rapid turnaround.
  • All Doors Closed: Closes and arms all doors prior to pushback.
  • Auto Doors: On supported airliners, cycles door modes through automatic sequencing for departure and arrival.

docs.title: Airliner Ground Equipment
docs.text:
• Wheel Chocks: Place or remove main gear chocks. (Ensure parking brake is set before removing chocks).
  • Ground Power Unit (GPU): Connects the ground electrical power cart.
  • HP Air: Connects the high-pressure pneumatic air cart for engine start.
  • LP Air: Connects the low-pressure air conditioning cart for cabin pre-conditioning.
  • Passenger Stairs: Summons forward and aft boarding stairs for non-jetway stands.
  • Service Trucks: Drives catering scissor-lift trucks to galley service doors.

docs.title: General Aviation Operations
docs.text: When operating general aviation aircraft (such as the Diamond DA42 or Cessna 172), the application switches to tailored GA ground equipment and cabin controls:

docs.title: Cabin & Canopy Access
docs.text: • Canopy / Cabin Doors: Open or close the pilot, passenger, and baggage doors.

docs.title: General Aviation Servicing Equipment
docs.text:
• Wheel Chocks: Secure the aircraft wheels while parked.
  • Tie-Downs: Secure the wing and tail tie-down ropes for ramp parking.
  • Pitot & Static Covers: Install or remove protective pitot tube covers and static port flags.
  • Gust Locks: Engage or release physical control surface gust locks.
  • Engine Covers: Place protective thermal or debris cowl plugs over engine intakes.
  • Engine Pre-Heater: Activate ground engine pre-heating for cold weather operations.
  • Fuel Grounding Cable: Connect or disconnect the static grounding cable prior to refueling.

docs.title: Web Browser
docs.text:
The Web Browser application integrates a full-featured web browser directly onto the cockpit tablet screen.

Flight crews can consult real-time aviation resources, live information, and online operational documentation without leaving the simulator cockpit.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Multi-Tab Browsing: Open, switch between, and manage multiple tabs concurrently with automatic session persistence across flights.
  • Unified Omnibar & Search: Direct web address entry with integrated search (Google or DuckDuckGo).
  • Bookmarks System: Save and organize your favorite aviation websites with a toggleable quick-access bookmarks bar.
  • On-Screen Virtual Keyboard: Built-in touchscreen keyboard with full alphanumeric and numeric keypad modes for in-cockpit typing.
  • Desktop Browser Handoff: Tap the Desktop button to open complex web tasks or checkout links in your computer's native browser.

docs.title: 1. Address Bar
docs.text:
• Direct URL Entry: Tap the address bar, type any web address (e.g., windy.com or https://maps.google.com), and press Enter or the arrow button.
  • Search Queries: Type any search query (e.g., LFPG METAR or EHAM chart notes) to search using your configured search engine.
  • Search Engine Selection: Set your preferred search engine (Google or DuckDuckGo) in the Settings application.

docs.title: 2. Tab Management
docs.text:
• New Tab: Tap the + button in the tab bar to open a new tab.
  • Switch Tabs: Tap any tab in the header to switch to it instantly.
  • Close Tab: Tap the × button on any tab to close it.
  • Session Persistence: Open tabs, navigation history, and last active addresses are saved automatically and restored when launching X-Plane.

docs.title: 3. Bookmarks Bar
docs.text:
• Bookmark Current Page: Tap the Star icon in the address bar to add the active page to your bookmarks.
  • Toggle Bookmarks Bar: Tap the Bookmark icon in the top toolbar to show or hide the quick-access bookmark strip.
  • Custom Bookmarks: Add custom shortcuts with custom titles and URLs using the + Add Bookmark button.
  • Edit & Remove: Tap the pencil icon on any bookmark to edit its title/URL, or tap the trash icon to remove it.

docs.title: 4. On-Screen Virtual Keyboard
docs.text:
When interacting with the tablet in the 3D cockpit without reaching for your physical keyboard:

  1. Tap the Keyboard icon in the browser toolbar, or click into any web text input field.
  2. The virtual keyboard will slide up from the bottom of the screen.
  3. Switch between standard QWERTY and numeric/symbol keypads as needed.
  4. Tap the close button or anywhere outside the keyboard to dismiss it.

docs.title: External Views & Remote Devices
docs.text: The built-in web browser is rendered exclusively on the 3D cockpit tablet display inside X-Plane.

docs.title: Charts & Navigation
docs.text:
The Charts application displays aerodrome diagrams, departure routes (SID), terminal arrivals (STAR), and approach plates directly on the tablet screen with real-time aircraft position overlay.

Important Note: A Navigraph subscription is required for this application to work.

docs.title: Navigraph Account Linking
docs.text:
AlphaFloor EFB integrates directly with Navigraph Charts:

  1. Open the Charts or the Settings application on the EFB.
  2. If not previously signed in, tap Log in to Navigraph.
  3. A Navigraph login page is displayed. You can log in with your Navigraph credentials.
  4. The tablet will automatically refresh and connect to the worldwide Jeppesen chart database.

docs.title: 1. Pinned Airports
docs.text:
When a SimBrief flight plan is active, AlphaFloor EFB automatically pins your:

  • Departure Airport
  • Destination Airport
  • Enroute Alternate(s)

Tap any pinned airport badge at the top of the screen to view its chart directory.

docs.title: 2. Manual Airport Search
docs.text:
To search for any global airport:

  1. Tap the search bar in the top navigation header.
  2. Type the 4-letter ICAO code (e.g., EGLL, EDDF, KSFO).
  3. Press Enter to view all available charts.

docs.title: 3. Chart Categories
docs.text:
Charts are organized into standard operational tabs:

  • APT: Airport diagrams, parking stand charts, low-visibility taxi routes, and hot spot advisories.
  • DEP: Standard Instrument Departures.
  • ARR: Standard Terminal Arrival Routes.
  • APP: Instrument Approach Procedures (ILS, RNP, RNAV, VOR, Visual).
  • REF: Noise abatement, special departure procedures, and airport general notes.

docs.title: Interactive Chart Viewer Features
docs.text:
• Moving Map Position Overlay: On georeferenced taxi diagrams and approach plates, a magenta aircraft symbol indicates your exact real-time position and heading.
  • Day & Night Themes: Toggle between high-contrast daylight mode and dim night mode to preserve night cockpit vision.
  • Zoom & Pan Controls: Use your mouse click-drag in the cockpit, or natural pinch-to-zoom gestures on external tablets.
  • Rotation: Rotate landscape and portrait charts with the 90-degree rotate button.

docs.title: Moving Map & Georeferenced Enroute Overlay
docs.text: AlphaFloor EFB overlays your planned flight plan route and real-time simulator GPS telemetry onto a fluid, interactive navigation map:

docs.title: Checklists
docs.text: The Checklists application provides interactive operational checklists designed to streamline cockpit workflows, reinforce SOP adherence, and enhance situational awareness. Checklists are automatically loaded to match the active aircraft type.

docs.title: Airframe-Tailored Checklist Flows
docs.text: AlphaFloor EFB includes built-in operational checklist flows tailored to specific aircraft families:

docs.title: 1. Commercial Airliner Flow
docs.text:
1. Cockpit Preparation
  2. Before Start
  3. After Start
  4. Taxi
  5. Line Up
  6. Approach
  7. Landing
  8. After Landing
  9. Parking
  10. Securing the Aircraft

docs.title: 2. Diamond DA42 Flow
docs.text:
1. Before Start
  2. Engine Start
  3. After Start
  4. Taxi
  5. Before Take-Off
  6. After Take-Off
  7. Descent & Approach
  8. Landing & After Landing

docs.title: 3. Cessna 172 Flow
docs.text:
1. Preflight
  2. Engine Start
  3. Before Taxi
  4. Taxi
  5. Engine Runup
  6. Before Takeoff
  7. Takeoff
  8. Climb
  9. Cruise
  10. Descent
  11. Before Landing
  12. Final Landing
  13. After Landing
  14. Engine Shutdown
  15. Securing Aircraft

docs.title: Operating Checklists
docs.text:
• Checking Items: Click or tap any checklist line item. The item highlights in green with a checkmark.
  • Sub-Items: Complex procedural checks include expandable sub-items that can be verified individually.
  • Headers & Reminders: Clear section dividers and prominent reminder notes highlight operational limitations.
  • Phase Navigation: Use the sidebar to quickly navigate between flight phases as your flight progresses.
  • Resetting Checklists: Click Reset Phase to clear items in the active phase, or Reset All to reset the entire checklist suite for a new flight leg.

docs.title: Custom Checklists (user_checklists.json)
docs.text:
You can customize checklists to match your airline's specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) or virtual flight operations:

  1. Locate the example template in your plugin directory: 
    X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins/AlphaFloorEFB/user_checklists.json.example
  2. Make a copy of this file and rename it to: 
    user_checklists.json
  3. Open user_checklists.json in any text editor. It supports section titles, challenge/response pairs, sub-items, section headers, and reminder notes:
[
  {
    "title": "Cockpit Preparation",
    "items": [
      { "item": "Gear Pins & Covers", "check": "REMOVED" },
      { "item": "Fuel Quantity", "check": "___ KG/LB" },
      { "item": "Signs", "check": "ON" }
    ]
  },
  {
    "title": "Before Take-Off",
    "items": [
      { "item": "LIMITATION", "check": "100% = 5 MIN MAXIMUM", "reminder": true },
      {
        "item": "ECAM Memo",
        "check": "T.O. No Blue",
        "subitems": [
          "Auto Brk MAX",
          "Signs On",
          "Flaps Conf 1+F",
          "Spoilers Armed"
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
]

docs.title: Documents Viewer
docs.text: The Documents application allows flight crews to view PDF flight documentation, Quick Reference Handbooks (QRH), airline Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and Flight Crew Operating Manuals (FCOM) directly on the tablet screen.

docs.title: Adding Your Own Documents
docs.text:
To make custom PDF documents available in the EFB:

  1. Navigate to one of the following folders:
  2. Your AlphaFloor EFB plugin folder: X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins/AlphaFloorEFB/documents/
  3. Per-aircraft folder: X-Plane 12/Aircraft/[aircraft_folder]/efb_docs/
  4. Create the folders if they don't exist
  5. Copy any standard .pdf files into the directory (e.g., A320_QRH.pdf, Company_SOP.pdf, Route_Briefing.pdf).
  6. Open or refresh the Documents application on the EFB. Your files will appear in the document library.

docs.title: Document Viewer Controls
docs.text:
• Document Library: Lists all available PDF, allowing to pin favorites for quick access.
  • Page Navigation:
  • Tap the Next Page and Previous Page arrows to flip pages.
  • Use the Page Jump box to type a specific page number and press Enter.
  • Zoom & Pan: Adjust reading scale using the Zoom In/Out controls. Pan using the mouse grab.

docs.title: Landing Performance Calculator
docs.text: The Landing Performance application calculates approach reference speeds, stopping distances, factoring margins, and engine-out go-around climb gradients for arrival planning.

docs.title: Landing Calculation Workflow
docs.text:
Prior to descent (during the descent and arrival briefing):

  1. Airport & Runway Selection: Select your planned destination or diversion aerodrome and landing runway. Runway length, slope, and elevation are loaded automatically.
  2. Weather & Runway Surface Conditions: Enter surface wind, temperature, barometric pressure (in hPa or inHg), and runway condition (Dry, Good, Medium, Poor).
  3. Aircraft Landing Weight: Confirm estimated landing weight (in Tonnes or 1000 lbs according to your configured unit system in Settings). When syncing with SimBrief, planned landing weights from LBS or KG flight plans are imported seamlessly.
  4. Flaps & Deceleration Devices: Select landing flap setting, reverse thrust mode, and wheel braking method (Autobrake Low/Medium/Max or Manual).
  5. Compute Performance: Tap Compute to evaluate arrival performance.
  6. Review Results:
  7. Approach Speed ($V_{APP}$): Target approach speed including wind correction.
  8. Landing Distances: Operational landing distance (unfactored) and dispatch factored landing distance.
  9. Runway Margin: Visual stop margin indicator showing remaining runway beyond rollout.
  10. Engine-Out Go-Around Gradient: Computes the single-engine missed approach climb gradient percentage to verify compliance with published missed approach procedure gradient requirements.

docs.title: 1. License Management
docs.text:
• License Status: Displays your current entitlement:
  • Licensed (Full Lifetime Version)
  • Active Free Trial (X days remaining)
  • Activate License: Input your purchased license key (key/XXXX) and click Activate.

docs.title: 2. Aircraft Unit System
docs.text:
• Unit System: Select your aircraft's unit system:
  • Metric (kg, m): Weights in Kilograms (kg) and Tonnes (t), barometric pressure in hPa.
  • Imperial (lbs, ft): Weights in Pounds (lbs) and 1000 lbs (klbs), barometric pressure in inHg.
  • This setting defines the default unit system used by the Performance and Weight & Balance applications.

docs.title: 3. Account Integrations
docs.text:
• SimBrief: Enter and save your SimBrief Pilot ID or username to automatically load dispatch flight plans.
  • Navigraph: View your Navigraph Charts connection status, authenticate, or sign out.

docs.title: 4. Web Browser Settings
docs.text: • Default Search Engine: Choose your preferred search provider for the Web Browser address bar (Google or DuckDuckGo).

docs.title: 5. Charts Mode
docs.text: • Charts Mode: Toggle between dark and bright chart background.

docs.title: 6. Remote Access (Wi-Fi LAN Streaming)
docs.text:
• Server Status: Indicates whether the local network server is active.
  • Local LAN Address: Displays the exact URL to type into your external tablet or phone browser (e.g., http://192.168.1.42:40899).
  • Connection QR Code: Scan the QR code with your mobile camera to open the EFB interface without typing IP addresses.
  • Port Configuration: Change the default listening port (40899) if you have other software utilizing that port.

docs.title: 7. Synchronize EFBs
docs.text: • Synchronize EFBs: Enable or disable synchronization between all connected EFBs.

docs.title: 8. Virtual Keyboard
docs.text: • Virtual Keyboard: Enable or disable the in-cockpit on-screen virtual keyboard when selecting text or numeric inputs. When set to OFF, selecting an input field allows typing exclusively through your physical hardware keyboard without displaying an on-screen keyboard overlay.

docs.title: SimBrief Operational Flight Plan (OFP)
docs.text: The SimBrief OFP application integrates with your SimBrief account to display your full operational flight plan, fuel calculations, route waypoints, and weather reports directly in the cockpit.

docs.title: Setting Up Your SimBrief Account
docs.text:
1. Open the SimBrief app from the EFB home screen (or navigate to Settings).
  2. Enter your SimBrief Username or numeric Pilot ID.
  3. Tap Save & Fetch.
  4. AlphaFloor EFB will query the SimBrief API and load your latest dispatch package. Your username is saved locally, so you only need to enter it once.

docs.title: 1. Flight Overview
docs.text:
Displays critical flight details at the top of the screen:

  • Flight Number & Call sign (e.g., AFR1234)
  • Departure & Arrival Airports with scheduled departure times and estimated flight duration
  • Planned Runways & ATC Filed Route: Filed route text includes planned departure and arrival runways for streamlined FMC/MCDU flight plan entry.
  • Alternate Airport(s) with distance and reserve fuel requirements
  • Cruising Altitude / Initial Flight Level (e.g., FL350)
  • Airframe Type & Registration

docs.title: 2. Fuel & Weight Breakdown
docs.text:
Summarizes planned fuel figures and weights for easy cross-checking with your MCDU. The app automatically detects and displays all quantities in either Kilograms (KGS) or Pounds (LBS) according to the units selected in your dispatch flight plan:

  • Block Fuel: Total fuel required on board before pushback.
  • Trip Fuel: Calculated burn for the planned route.
  • Contingency & Reserve Fuel: FAR/EASA regulatory reserves.
  • Alternate Fuel: Fuel required to divert to the planned alternate.
  • Zero Fuel Weight (ZFW): Planned aircraft empty weight plus payload.
  • Takeoff Weight (TOW): Calculated weight at brake release.

docs.title: 3. Route Navigation Log (Navlog)
docs.text:
Provides a scrollable navigation log listing:

  • Every airway, fix, and waypoint along the cleared routing.
  • Planned flight levels.
  • Forecast winds aloft (direction and speed).
  • Leg distance and estimated time.
  • Estimated Fuel On-board and editable Actual Fuel On-board entries to track fuel burn during flight.

docs.title: 4. Weather, METAR & TAF
docs.text:
Aggregates real-time weather reports for all airports along your itinerary:

  • Departure Weather: Raw METAR, decoded wind, altimeter setting (QNH/inHg), temperature, and runway surface reports.
  • Destination Weather: Current conditions and terminal aerodrome forecasts (TAF).
  • Enroute Alternates: Quick-reference weather cards for emergency diversion planning.

docs.title: 5. Full PDF Briefing Package
docs.text: View the complete, multi-page operational flight plan document formatted exactly as generated by your airline dispatch:

docs.title: Takeoff Performance Calculator
docs.text: The Takeoff Performance application computes precise departure performance figures, optimal thrust settings, and reference takeoff speeds.

docs.title: Takeoff Calculation Workflow
docs.text:
1. Airport & Runway Selection: Enter the 4-letter ICAO code for your departure aerodrome. Select the active runway or designated intersection departure. Available runway lengths (TORA, TODA, ASDA) and elevation update automatically.
  2. Atmospheric Conditions: Verify surface wind direction/speed, outside air temperature (OAT), and barometric altimeter setting (in hPa or inHg).
  3. Aircraft Configuration: Confirm takeoff gross weight (in Tonnes or 1000 lbs), air conditioning packs status (ON/OFF), anti-ice configuration (ENG or ENG+WING), and desired flap setting.
  4. Compute Performance: Tap Compute to execute the calculation.
  5. Review Results:
  6. Assumed / FLEX Temperature: Maximum permissible thrust reduction temperature.
  7. V-Speeds: Decision speed ($V_1$), Rotation speed ($V_R$), and Engine-out safety speed ($V_2$).
  8. Trim & Speeds: Recommended pitch trim (THS) and clean climb speed (Green Dot).
  9. Runway Margins: Required takeoff roll distance and stop margin remaining.
  10. MCDU / FMGS Insertion: Tap Insert in MCDU to transfer computed V-speeds and FLEX temperature directly into the aircraft FMGS scratchpad on supported aircraft.

[!NOTE] Due to aircraft FMGS dataref limitations, the takeoff flap and pitch trim setting (FLAPS/THS, e.g. 1/UP0.5) cannot be inserted automatically via datarefs. Enter this figure manually into line select key 3R on the MCDU PERF TAKEOFF page.

docs.title: Weather
docs.text: The Weather application provides enroute radar imagery and vertical atmospheric cross-sections along your planned flight route.

docs.title: Display Modes
docs.text:
The view selector located in the top-right header allows switching between three viewing layouts:

  • Split: Displays both the 2D interactive route map and the vertical atmospheric profile.
  • Map: Full-screen 2D navigation map with precipitation radar, flight plan routing, waypoints, and live aircraft position.
  • Profile: Full-screen vertical cross-section displaying cloud layers.

docs.title: Interactive 2D Weather Map
docs.text:
The map displays your cleared routing alongside live radar:

  • Flight Route: Depicts departure airport, intermediate waypoints, destination airport, and planned alternates.
  • Aircraft Position: Real-time magenta aircraft symbol indicating your current GPS coordinates and true heading.
  • Precipitation Radar: Displays radar reflectivity across light, moderate, heavy, and severe convective precipitation bands.

docs.title: Vertical Atmospheric Profile
docs.text: The profile view plots a longitudinal cross-section of your flight from takeoff to landing, mapped against pressure altitude (Surface up to FL450):

docs.title: 1. Flight Trajectory & Live Position
docs.text:
• Planned Flight Levels: Depicts the step-climb profile calculated in your SimBrief OFP.
  • Live Aircraft Badge: A cyan aircraft symbol tracks your actual barometric altitude and along-track distance in real time.

docs.title: 2. Meteorological Layers & Hazards
docs.text:
• Cloud Layers: Visualizes cloud coverage with base and top altitudes, shaded according to cloud coverage percentage.
  • Freezing Level (0°C Isotherm): Marked as a dashed amber line indicating the zero-degree boundary throughout the route.
  • Icing: Warning indicators highlight flight segments where supercooled moisture and freezing temperatures present icing hazards.

docs.title: 3. Interactive Atmospheric Sounding Overlay
docs.text:
Scrubbing your cursor or tapping anywhere along the route reveals a detailed sounding card for that specific point:

  • Distance: Cumulative nautical miles from departure and remaining distance to destination.
  • Nearest Waypoint & Airway: Closest navigation fix along the cleared route.
  • Planned Altitude: Scheduled flight level from the flight plan.
  • Point Cloud Coverage: Indicates whether the cursor is in clear air or inside a cloud deck (In Cloud with local coverage percentage).
  • Cloud Layers Breakdown: Vertical listing of all cloud decks present at that waypoint, including layer index, base altitude, top altitude, and coverage percentage.

docs.title: Forecast Timeline & 4D Flight Sync
docs.text:
The forecast toolbar at the bottom of the screen allows evaluating weather evolution over time:

  • 4D Flight Sync: Calculates atmospheric soundings dynamically matched to your aircraft's estimated time of arrival (ETA) at each waypoint along the route, taking into account departure time and elapsed flight progress.
  • Now: Instantaneous snapshot of current weather conditions across the entire route.
  • +3H / +6H / +12H: Forward-looking synoptic forecast projections, useful for assessing front movements and terminal weather developments for long-haul flights or delayed departures.

docs.title: Data Providers & Rate Limiting
docs.text:
• Precipitation Radar: Global composite reflectivity tiles provided by RainViewer.
  • Atmospheric Soundings: The profile view relies on the Open-Meteo API for numerical weather prediction soundings along the flight route.

Weather data is automatically cached per flight to minimize external network requests. Open-Meteo imposes request rate limits; if request limits are reached or the service is temporarily unavailable, a "Weather data temporarily unavailable" overlay is displayed until the rate-limit window resets or connectivity is restored.

docs.title: Weight & Balance
docs.text: The Weight & Balance application manages aircraft passenger distribution, cargo hold loading, fuel uplift, and Center of Gravity (CG) envelope calculations.

docs.title: 1. Extended Airframe Profiles
docs.text: For aircraft with dedicated airframe profiles (including Airbus A319, A320, A321, A330, and A340): * Interactive Cabin Seat Map: Board passengers by cabin zones or individually using the visual seat map. * Cargo Hold Distribution: Distribute freight across forward, aft, and bulk compartments. * Dynamic CG Flight Envelope: Real-time Center of Gravity (% MAC) calculations plotted against certified forward and aft envelope limits for Zero Fuel Weight (ZFW), Takeoff Weight (TOW), and Landing Weight (LAW). * THS Pitch Trim Calculation: Computes the exact stabilizer pitch trim setting (e.g., UP 1.2 or DN 0.5) based on computed TOW CG.

docs.title: 2. Universal Aircraft Mode
docs.text: For all other X-Plane 12 aircraft: * Utilizes standard X-Plane payload stations and fuel tanks. * Allows reviewing total payload, passenger weight, cargo, and fuel distribution. * Enables one-click payload and fuel loading from SimBrief dispatch plans.

docs.title: Configuration Workflow
docs.text:
1. Unit System Selection: Select your preferred unit system (KG or LBS) using the header toggle. The app automatically defaults to the system specified in your active SimBrief OFP, or the default configured in Settings.
  2. Passenger & Cargo Loading: Adjust passenger count, cabin distribution, and cargo weights. When clicking Load SimBrief, planned fuel and cargo figures are imported and converted automatically.
  3. Fuel Uplift: Set the desired fuel quantity across available fuel tanks.
  4. Envelope Verification: Verify that the calculated Zero Fuel Weight CG and Takeoff Weight CG (% MAC) remain securely within certified operational limits.
  5. Apply to Aircraft: Tap Apply to Aircraft to synchronize fuel and payload weights directly into the simulator.

docs.title: Interactive Seat Map
docs.text: For supported aircraft, tap the seat map toggle to inspect and adjust passenger seating arrangements dynamically:
